sections.h2: Telecom provisioning, done in one place

blocks.text: Fulfilment Manager handles **telecom provisioning**: it carries out service orders in the network. An activation, a suspension or a plan change leaves CRM or billing, reaches the right network element and comes back confirmed.

At most operators, **provisioning in telecom** is done by scripts and middleware built in-house, and many fiber operators push changes straight to their OLTs that way. Billing-day suspensions flood the network. Nobody can prove which orders completed, and billing and the network drift apart.

Fulfilment Manager replaces those scripts with one product. It takes orders from CRM and billing and carries them out on OLTs, subscriber databases (HLR and HSS), online charging, policy control and AAA.

blocks.text: Also known as: FFM, Activator, **service activation**, **service provisioning**, push-based access control
Each order is confirmed per customer. Billing knows that a suspension reached the line, and care knows that an activation finished.
A command that fails retries on its own. Operators can review, pause and retry anything that is pending.

sections.h2: Billing day without flooding the network

blocks.text: Suspensions and restorations arrive in bulk after each billing run. Fulfilment Manager paces them, so your network keeps up.
Each order still goes to the right network element and comes back with its own result.

sections.h2: Keep pushing configuration to your OLTs

blocks.text: If you provision by pushing configuration to the OLT, you keep doing so. There is no rebuild around a BNG.
Pull-based AAA can be added later behind the same interface, when you are ready.

Above it sit CRM, order management and billing, Alepo's or your own. Below it sit OLTs, subscriber databases (HLR and HSS), online charging, policy control, AAA and service platforms, over REST and SOAP.
Mobile operators, MVNOs and MVNEs use it the same way, to activate one service across several network elements.

items.a: It carries out service orders on the network. Activations, suspensions, restorations and plan changes from CRM or billing reach the right network element, and each one is confirmed per customer.

items.q: Do we have to redesign the network around a BNG?
items.a: No. Fiber operators that push configuration to the OLT keep doing so. Pull-based AAA can be added later behind the same interface.

items.q: What happens when a command fails?
items.a: It retries on its own. Operators can review, pause and retry anything that is pending.

items.q: How does it handle billing day?
items.a: It paces bulk suspensions and restorations so the network is not flooded, and returns a result for each order.

items.q: Which systems does it connect to?
items.a: CRM and order management above, plus billing. OLTs, subscriber databases (HLR and HSS), online charging, policy control, AAA and service platforms below, over REST and SOAP.

blocks.text: Your team installs Fulfilment Manager in containers, one standard way, from the same automated guide as every Alepo product. Upgrades stay small.

When something needs fixing, the patch goes only to the component affected, with rollback ready, so your maintenance window stays short and nothing else has to be upgraded at the same time. Fulfilment Manager runs on Kubernetes in your environment, operated by your team or by Alepo, with 24x7 support from GTAC.
The build you test and see demoed is the build that goes live.
